title.zh: 卷八十六 列傳第四十六 殷孝祖 劉勔
title.en: Volume 86 Biographies 46: Yin Xiaozu, Liu Mian
title.raw: 卷八十六 列傳第四十六 殷孝祖 劉勔 Volume 86 Biographies 46: Yin Xiaozu, Liu Mian

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十六 殷孝祖 劉勔

translations.literal: Biography 46: Yin Xiaozu, Liu Mian
translations.idiomatic: Biography Number Forty-Six: Yin Xiaozu and Liu Mian

sentences.zh: 殷孝祖，陳郡長平人也。

translations.literal: Yin Xiaozu was a native of Changping in Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xiaozu came from Changping in Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖羨，晉光祿勳。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xian was Jin Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xian had served as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 父祖並不達。

translations.literal: His father and grandfather both did not attain success.
translations.idiomatic: Neither his father nor his grandfather had risen to distinction.

sentences.zh: 孝祖少誕節，好酒色，有氣幹。

translations.literal: Xiaozu from youth was unrestrained in conduct, fond of wine and women, and possessed force of character.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xiaozu was free-spirited and fond of wine and women, yet he had real force of character.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉末，為奉朝請，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanjia era under Emperor Wu of Song, he was a court attendant and Extraordinary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuanjia reign of Emperor Wu, he served as a court attendant and as an extraordinary attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 世祖以其有武用，除奮武將軍、濟北太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, seeing his military ability, appointed him General Who Stirs Martial Valor and Governor of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu valued his military talent and made him General Who Stirs Martial Valor and governor of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 入為積射將軍。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as General of Accumulated Archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as General of Accumulated Archery.

sentences.zh: 大明初，索虜寇青州，上遣孝祖北援，受刺史顏師伯節度，累與虜戰，頻大破之，事在師伯傳。

translations.literal: Early in the Daming era, the Northern Wei raided Qing Province; the emperor sent Xiaozu north to reinforce, placed under the command of Governor Yan Shibo; he repeatedly fought the barbarians and often routed them—the account is in Shibo's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daming, when the Wei struck Qing Province, the court sent Xiaozu north under Governor Yan Shibo's command; he fought them again and again and won repeated victories, as told in Shibo's biography.

sentences.zh: 還授太子旅賁中郎將，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: On his return he was made Central Commander of the Heir's Brave Escort and additionally General of the Dragon Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he was appointed central commander of the heir's brave escort and given the additional rank of General of the Dragon Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕據廣陵為逆，孝祖隸沈慶之攻誕，又有戰功，遷西陽王子尚撫軍、寧朔將軍、南濟陰太守。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingling Dan held Guangling in rebellion, Xiaozu served under Shen Qingzhi in the attack on Dan, again won merit in battle, and was transferred to staff of the Heir Prince of Xiyang Zishang's Pacification Army, made General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Southern Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Dan of Jingling seized Guangling in revolt, Xiaozu fought under Shen Qingzhi against him and won further distinction; he was then assigned to Prince Zishang of Xiyang's pacification staff as General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Southern Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 出為盱眙太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Xuyi, his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to govern Xuyi while retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 還為虎賁中郎將，仍除寧朔將軍、陽平、東平二郡太守。

translations.literal: On return he was made Central Commander of the Tiger Guard and concurrently appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of the two commanderies Yangping and Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he became a central commander of the tiger guard and was also made General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Yangping and Dongping.

sentences.zh: 又遷濟南、南郡，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was further transferred to Jinan and Nan Commandery, his generalship as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was later moved to govern Jinan and Nan Commandery, still holding the same general's title.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和元年，以本號督兗州諸軍事、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe under the Deposed Former Emperor, with his existing title he was made Commander-in-Chief of Yanzhou military affairs and Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe under the Deposed Emperor, he was placed in command of all Yan Province forces and made its governor, keeping his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 太宗初即位，四方反叛，孝祖外甥司徒參軍潁川葛僧韶建議銜命徵孝祖入朝，上遣之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming first took the throne, rebellion broke out on all sides; Xiaozu's nephew, Secretariat Army Staff Officer Ge Sengshao of Yingchuan, proposed that an imperial order summon Xiaozu to court, and the emperor sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Emperor Ming's accession, the realm rose in revolt; Xiaozu's nephew Ge Sengshao, a staff officer of the Secretariat, urged that an imperial messenger summon Xiaozu to the capital, and the emperor dispatched him.

sentences.zh: 時徐州刺史薛安都遣薛索兒等屯據津徑，僧韶間行得至，說孝祖曰：「景和兇狂，開闢未有，朝野危極，假命漏刻。

translations.literal: At that time Yanzhou Governor Xue An'du had sent Xue Suo'er and others to hold the ferry routes; Sengshao by secret paths reached him and said to Xiaozu: "Jinghe was ferocious and mad, unprecedented since the founding of the dynasty; court and countryside were in extreme peril, living on borrowed time."
translations.idiomatic: Xue An'du of Xu Province had posted Xue Suo'er and others along the ferry crossings, but Sengshao slipped through and told Xiaozu: "The Jinghe reign was savage beyond anything since the dynasty's founding; the whole realm teetered on the edge of ruin, its life measured in hours."

sentences.zh: 主上聖德天挺，神武在躬，曾不浹辰，夷凶翦暴，更造天地，未足為言。

translations.literal: Our lord's sagely virtue was heaven-bestowed, divine martial prowess in his person; in less than a full day he quelled the wicked and cut down the violent, remaking heaven and earth—words hardly suffice.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor's virtue is heaven-sent and his martial prowess is in his very person; in less than a day he has crushed the wicked and remade the realm—no words can do justice to it.

sentences.zh: 國亂朝危，宜立長生，公卿百辟，人無異議，泰平之隆，非旦則夕。

translations.literal: The state was in turmoil and the court in peril; a mature ruler ought to be established; among ministers and officials none dissented; the grandeur of great peace would come not in the morning but by evening.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm in chaos, a mature sovereign has been raised up; ministers and officials are of one mind, and an age of peace is only days away.

sentences.zh: 而群小相煽，構造無端，貪利幼弱，競懷希望。

translations.literal: Yet petty men stirred one another on, fabricating groundless plots, greedy for profit from a young and weak ruler, each nursing hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet petty men are stirring one another up, inventing pretexts and hoping to profit from a child on the throne.

sentences.zh: 使天道助逆，群凶事申，則主幼時艱，權柄不一，兵難互起，豈有自容之地。

translations.literal: If heaven's way aided the rebels and the wicked succeeded, then with a young lord times would be hard, power not unified, and military troubles would arise in turn—where would there be room for oneself?
translations.idiomatic: If fortune favors the rebels and they prevail, a child emperor will mean hard times, divided authority, and endless wars—where will any of us find safety?

sentences.zh: 舅少有立功之志，長以氣節成名，若便能控濟、河義勇，還奉朝廷，非唯匡主靜亂，乃可以垂名竹帛。

translations.literal: Uncle, you from youth had the will to achieve merit and in maturity were famed for integrity; if you could now rally the righteous volunteers of the Ji and Yellow rivers and return to serve the court, you would not only steady the ruler and quell disorder but also leave your name on silk and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle, you have long wished to win distinction and are known for your integrity; if you can rally the loyal forces along the Ji and Yellow rivers and return to the court, you will not only save the throne and end the turmoil—you will win a name that lasts in history.

sentences.zh: 」孝祖具問朝廷消息，僧韶隨方酬譬，並陳兵甲精強，主上欲委以前驅之任。

translations.literal: " Xiaozu questioned him fully on court news; Sengshao answered as occasion required and also declared the troops and armor strong, that the emperor wished to entrust him with the vanguard command.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaozu pressed him for every detail of the court's situation; Sengshao answered point by point, assured him the army was strong, and said the emperor meant to give him the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 孝祖即日棄妻子，率文武二千人隨僧韶還都。

translations.literal: That very day Xiaozu abandoned wife and children and led two thousand civil and military followers with Sengshao back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Xiaozu left his family behind and marched two thousand officers and men back to the capital with Sengshao.

sentences.zh: 時普天同逆，朝廷唯保丹陽一郡，而永世縣尋又反叛。

translations.literal: At that time all under heaven joined the rebellion; the court held only Danyang Commandery, and soon Yongshi County also rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The whole realm had turned against the throne; the court clung only to Danyang, and before long Yongshi County rose as well.

sentences.zh: 義興賊垂至延陵，內外憂危，咸欲奔散。

translations.literal: Rebels from Yixing were about to reach Yanling; within and without there was dread, and all wished to flee and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Yixing were closing on Yanling; panic spread inside and out, and everyone wanted to run.

sentences.zh: 孝祖忽至，眾力不少，並傖楚壯士，人情於是大安。

translations.literal: Xiaozu suddenly arrived; his force was not small, all northern and Chu stalwarts, and popular feeling then greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozu appeared without warning, he brought a sizable force of northern and Chu veterans, and morale at once steadied.

sentences.zh: 進孝祖號冠軍，假節、督前鋒諸軍事，遣向虎檻，拒對南賊。

translations.literal: Xiaozu was advanced in title to Champion General, given the staff of authority and command of vanguard military affairs, and sent toward Tiger Cage to confront the southern rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Champion General, given the staff of command over the vanguard, and sent to Tiger Cage to hold the southern rebels at bay.

sentences.zh: 御仗先有諸葛亮筒袖鎧帽，二十五石弩射之不能入，上悉以賜孝祖。

translations.literal: Among the imperial armory were Zhuge Liang-style tube-sleeve armor and caps that a twenty-five-stone crossbow could not pierce; the emperor gave them all to Xiaozu.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial stores held Zhuge Liang-style tube-sleeve armor and helmets proof even against a twenty-five-stone crossbow; the emperor gave the whole set to Xiaozu.

sentences.zh: 孝祖負其誠節，凌轢諸將，臺軍有父子兄弟在南者，孝祖並欲推治。

translations.literal: Xiaozu, relying on his loyal integrity, overbearing toward the generals, wished to investigate and punish all capital troops who had fathers, sons, or brothers in the south.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his own loyalty, Xiaozu rode roughshod over the other generals and even wanted to prosecute any capital soldier whose kin had sided with the rebels in the south.

sentences.zh: 由是人情乖離，莫樂為用。

translations.literal: Hence popular feeling turned away and none were glad to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: Men's hearts turned from him, and no one was eager to follow his lead.

sentences.zh: 進使持節、都督兗州、青、冀、幽四州諸軍事、撫軍將軍，刺史如故。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Yan, Qing, Ji, and You provinces' military affairs, and General Who Pacifies the Army, his governorship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to bearer of the imperial staff, commander of the four northern provinces, and General Who Pacifies the Army, while keeping his governorship.

sentences.zh: 時賊據赭圻，孝祖將進攻之，與大統王玄謨別，悲不自勝，眾並駭怪。

translations.literal: At that time the rebels held Zheqi; Xiaozu was about to attack them; when he parted from Grand Commander Wang Xuamo he could not master his grief, and all were startled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Zheqi, and as Xiaozu prepared to attack them he took leave of Grand Commander Wang Xuamo with uncontrollable grief, to everyone's astonishment.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年三月三日，與賊合戰，常以鼓蓋自隨，軍中人相謂曰：「殷統軍可謂死矣。

translations.literal: On the third day of the third month of the second year of Taishi, joining battle with the rebels, he always had drum and canopy follow him; men in the army said to one another: "Commander Yin may be called as good as dead."
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the third month of Taishi year two he met the rebels in battle, always keeping drum and canopy with him; soldiers muttered among themselves: "Commander Yin might as well be a dead man already."

sentences.zh: 今與賊交鋒，而以羽儀自標顯，若善射者十士攢射，欲不斃，得乎？

translations.literal: Now he clashes with the enemy yet marks himself with ceremonial insignia; if ten skilled archers shoot together, wishing not to be killed, can he succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Now he fights the enemy while flaunting his banners and canopy—if ten good archers loosed together, how could he hope to live?"

sentences.zh: 」是日，於陣為矢所中死，時年五十二。

translations.literal: " That day, in the battle line he was struck by an arrow and died, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: " That day he was struck down by an arrow in the front line. He was fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 追贈散騎常侍、征北將軍，持節、都督如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and General Who Campaigns North, staff and command unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and General Who Campaigns North, with his staff and command unchanged.

sentences.zh: 封秭歸縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zigui County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zigui with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 四年，追改封建安縣，諡曰忠侯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his fief was changed posthumously to Jian'an County; his posthumous title was Marquis Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year his fief was changed posthumously to Jian'an, with the posthumous title Loyal Marquis.

sentences.zh: 孝祖子悉為薛安都所殺，以從兄子慧達繼封。

translations.literal: All Xiaozu's sons were killed by Xue An'du; his cousin's son Huida succeeded to the fief.
translations.idiomatic: Xue An'du killed all of Xiaozu's sons; the marquisate passed to his cousin's son Huida.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi dynasty took the throne, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 劉勔，字伯猷，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Mian, styled Boyou, was a native of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian, styled Boyou, came from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 祖懷義，始興太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huaiyi was Governor of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huaiyi had been governor of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 父穎之，汝南、新蔡二郡太守，征林邑，遇疾卒。

translations.literal: His father Yingzhi was Governor of the two commanderies Runan and Xincai, campaigned against Linyi, and died of illness on the way.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingzhi governed Runan and Xincai, marched against Linyi, and died of illness on campaign.

sentences.zh: 勔少有志節，兼好文義。

translations.literal: Mian from youth had resolve and integrity and also loved literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Mian was principled and devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 家貧，為廣州增城令，廣州刺史劉道錫引為揚烈府主簿。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he became Magistrate of Zengcheng in Guang Province; Guangzhou Governor Liu Daoxi brought him in as chief clerk of the Yanglie commandery staff.
translations.idiomatic: Poor as his family was, he became magistrate of Zengcheng in Guang Province; Governor Liu Daoxi then took him on as chief clerk of his staff.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，索虜南侵，道錫遣勔奉使詣京都，太祖引見之，酬對稱旨，除寧遠將軍、綏遠太守。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia the Northern Wei invaded south; Daoxi sent Mian on embassy to the capital; Emperor Wu received him, his replies pleased the emperor, and he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Suiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year twenty-seven, when the Wei struck south, Daoxi sent Mian to the capital; Emperor Wu received him, was pleased with his answers, and made him General Who Pacifies the Distance and governor of Suiyuan.

sentences.zh: 元嘉末，蕭簡據廣州為亂，勔起義討之，燒其南門。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia, Xiao Jian held Guang Province in rebellion; Mian rose in loyal arms to attack him and burned the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yuanjia, when Xiao Jian seized Guang Province in revolt, Mian took up arms against him and burned the south gate.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史宗愨又命為軍府主簿，以功封大亭侯。

translations.literal: Guangzhou Governor Zong Que again appointed him chief clerk of the army staff; for merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dating.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zong Que made him chief clerk of the army staff, and for his service he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dating.

sentences.zh: 除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Extraordinary Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an extraordinary attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，荊、江反叛，宗愨以勔行寧朔將軍、湘東內史，領軍出安陸。

translations.literal: Early in Xiaojian, Jing and Jiang rebelled; Zong Que had Mian act as General Who Pacifies the North and Interior Lord of Xiangdong, leading troops out from Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaojian, when Jing and Jiang rose in revolt, Zong Que sent Mian out as General Who Pacifies the North and interior lord of Xiangdong, leading troops from Anlu.

sentences.zh: 會事平，以本號為晉康太守，又徙鬱林太守。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, with his existing title he was made Governor of Jinkang, then transferred to Governor of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion ended he was made governor of Jinkang under his existing rank, then moved to Yulin.

sentences.zh: 大明初還都，徐州刺史劉道隆請為寧朔司馬。

translations.literal: Early in Daming he returned to the capital; Xuzhou Governor Liu Daolong requested him as Pacify-the-North Army Major.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daming he returned to the capital, and Xu Province governor Liu Daolong asked to have him as army major of the Pacify-the-North command.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕據廣陵為逆，勔隨道隆受沈慶之節度，事平，封金城縣五等侯。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingling Dan held Guangling in rebellion, Mian followed Daolong under Shen Qingzhi's command; when affairs were settled he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Jincheng County.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Dan of Jingling seized Guangling, Mian served under Daolong in Shen Qingzhi's command; after the revolt was crushed he was made fifth-rank marquis of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 除西陽王子尚撫軍參軍，入直閣。

translations.literal: He was appointed Army Staff Officer to Prince of Xiyang Zishang's Pacification Army and entered attendance in the Inner Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He became a staff officer on Prince Zishang of Xiyang's pacification staff and entered service in the Inner Quarters.

sentences.zh: 先是，遣費沈伐陳檀，不克，乃除勔龍驤將軍、西江督護、鬱林太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fei Shen had been sent to attack Chen Tan and failed; then Mian was appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry, Protector of the West River, and Governor of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Fei Shen had been sent against Chen Tan without success; Mian was then made General of the Dragon Cavalry, protector of the West River, and governor of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 勔既至，率軍進討，隨宜翦定，大致名馬，并獻珊瑚連理樹，上甚悅。

translations.literal: When Mian arrived he led the army forward in attack, pacifying as circumstances required, gathered many famous horses, and also presented a coral intertwined-tree; the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mian arrived he led the campaign, pacifying the region as he went, gathered many fine horses, and presented a coral tree with intertwined branches; the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 還除新安王子鸞撫軍中兵參軍，遭母憂，不拜。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Central Army Staff Officer to Prince of Xin'an Ziluan's Pacification Army; he met with mother's mourning and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was named central army staff officer to Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, but declined the post when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，起為振威將軍、屯騎校尉，入直閣。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Former Emperor took the throne, Mian was recalled as General Who Shakes Might and Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry and entered the Inner Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, Mian was recalled as General Who Shakes Might and colonel of the garrison cavalry and again served in the Inner Quarters.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，加寧朔將軍，校尉如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Mian was additionally made General Who Pacifies the North, his colonelcy unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming succeeded, Mian was also made General Who Pacifies the North while keeping his colonel's rank.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史晉安王子勛為逆，四方回應，勔以本官領建平王景素輔國司馬，進據梁山。

translations.literal: Jiangzhou Governor Prince of Jin'an Zixun rebelled and the four quarters responded; Mian with his existing office also served as Pacify-the-State Army Major to Prince of Jianping Jingsu and advanced to hold Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zixun of Jin'an rebelled as governor of Jiang Province and the realm answered him, Mian took the additional post of army major to Prince Jingsu of Jianping and advanced to hold Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 會豫州刺史殷琰反叛，徵勔還都，假輔國將軍，率眾討琰，甲仗三十人入六門。

translations.literal: When Yuzhou Governor Yin Yan rebelled, Mian was summoned back to the capital, made acting General Who Assists the State, led troops to attack Yan, and entered the Six Gates with thirty armored attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Yan of Yu Province rebelled, Mian was recalled, given acting rank as General Who Assists the State, and sent against him with thirty armed attendants through the Six Gates.

sentences.zh: 復兼山陽王休祐驃騎司馬，餘如故。

translations.literal: He also concurrently served as Swift-Cavalry Army Major to Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made army major on Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang's swift-cavalry staff, with his other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 破琰將劉順於宛唐，杜叔寶於橫塘，事在琰傳。

translations.literal: He defeated Yan's generals Liu Shun at Wantang and Du Shubao at Hengtang—the account is in Yan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Yan's generals Liu Shun at Wantang and Du Shubao at Hengtang, as told in Yan's biography.

sentences.zh: 除輔國將軍、山陽王休祐驃騎諮議參軍、梁郡太守、假節，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Assists the State, Consulting Army Staff Officer to Prince Xiuyou's Swift-Cavalry Army, Governor of Liang Commandery, and acting staff bearer, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered General Who Assists the State, consulting staff officer to Prince Xiuyou's swift-cavalry command, governorship of Liang, and the acting staff of authority, but declined.

sentences.zh: 琰嬰城固守，自始春至於末冬，薛道標、龐孟虯並向壽陽，勔內攻外禦，戰無不捷。

translations.literal: Yan held the city in desperate defense from early spring to late winter; Xue Daobiao and Pang Mengjiao both marched on Shouyang; Mian attacked within and defended without, and in battle was never unsuccessful.
translations.idiomatic: Yan held out in the city from spring through winter while Xue Daobiao and Pang Mengjiao marched on Shouyang; Mian besieged within and fought off relief from without, winning every engagement.

sentences.zh: 善撫將帥，以寬厚為眾所依。

translations.literal: He was skilled in comforting generals and officers and relied on by all for his generosity.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his officers well, and men trusted him for his generosity.

sentences.zh: 將軍王廣之求勔所自乘馬，諸將帥並忿廣之叨冒，勸勔以法裁之，勔歡笑，即時解馬與廣之。

translations.literal: General Wang Guangzhi asked for Mian's own riding horse; the generals were all angry at Guangzhi's presumption and urged Mian to punish him by law; Mian laughed and at once gave him the horse.
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Guangzhi asked for Mian's own mount; the other commanders were furious at his boldness and urged Mian to punish him, but Mian only laughed and gave him the horse on the spot.

sentences.zh: 復除使持節、督廣、交二州諸軍事、平越中郎將、廣州刺史，將軍如故，不拜。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Guang and Jiao provinces' military affairs, General Who Pacifies the Yue, and Governor of Guang Province, his generalship unchanged, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was again offered the staff of command over Guang and Jiao, the title General Who Pacifies the Yue, and the governorship of Guang, but again declined.

sentences.zh: 及琰開門請降，勔約令三軍，不得妄動。

translations.literal: When Yan opened the gates to surrender, Mian bound the three armies not to act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan opened the gates to surrender, Mian strictly forbade his troops any disorder.

sentences.zh: 城內士民，秋毫無所失，百姓感悅，咸曰來蘇。

translations.literal: Within the city, commoners and gentry lost not a hair's breadth; the people were moved and pleased, all saying he had brought renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Not a thing was lost among the townspeople; the people were grateful and said he had brought them back to life.

sentences.zh: 百姓生為立碑。

translations.literal: While he still lived the people erected a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: The people raised a monument to him in his lifetime.

sentences.zh: 改督益、寧二州諸軍事、益州刺史，持節、將軍如故，又不拜。

translations.literal: His command was changed to Yi and Ning provinces' military affairs and Governor of Yi Province, staff and generalship as before, and again he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to command Yi and Ning and govern Yi, with the staff and his general's rank unchanged, and again he declined.

sentences.zh: 還京都，拜太子左衛率，封鄱陽縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he was made Left Leader of the Heir's Guard, enfeoffed as Marquis of Poyang County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the capital he was made left leader of the heir's guard and enfeoffed as Marquis of Poyang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 琰初求救索虜，虜大眾屯據汝南。

translations.literal: Yan at first had sought aid from the Northern Wei; a great barbarian host camped and held Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had first called on the Wei for help, and a large Wei force now held Runan.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，以勔為征虜將軍、督西討前鋒諸軍事，假節、置佐、本官如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi, Mian was made General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Commander-in-Chief of the western expedition vanguard, with acting staff, staff officers appointed, and his original offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi year three he was made General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and commander of the western vanguard, with acting staff and his other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 先是，常珍奇據汝南，與琰為逆，琰降，因據戍降虜，事在琰傳。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chang Zhenqi had held Runan and rebelled with Yan; when Yan surrendered, Zhenqi held the garrison and submitted to the barbarians—the account is in Yan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chang Zhenqi had held Runan and joined Yan's revolt; when Yan surrendered, Zhenqi kept the garrison and went over to the Wei, as told in Yan's biography.

sentences.zh: 至是引虜西河公、長社公攻圍輔國將軍、汝陰太守張景遠。

translations.literal: At this time they brought in the barbarian Prince of Xihe and Prince of Changshe to attack and besiege General Who Assists the State and Runan Governor Zhang Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: They now brought in the Wei princes of Xihe and Changshe to besiege General Zhang Jingyuan, governor of Yuyin.

sentences.zh: 景遠與軍主楊文萇拒擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Jingyuan with Army Commander Yang Wenchang resisted the attack and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan and his commander Yang Wenchang met them in battle and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 景遠尋病卒，太宗嘉其功，追贈冠軍將軍、豫州刺史，追封含洭縣男，食邑三百戶，以文萇代為汝陰太守。

translations.literal: Jingyuan soon died of illness; Emperor Ming praised his merit and posthumously gave him Champion General and Governor of Yu Province, posthumously enfeoffed him as Baron of Hanqu County with three hundred households, and made Wenchang acting Governor of Yuyin.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan soon died of illness; the emperor honored his service posthumously with the ranks of Champion General and governor of Yu, made him baron of Hanqu with three hundred households, and put Wenchang in his place as governor of Yuyin.

sentences.zh: 除勔右衛將軍，仍以為使持節、都督豫、司二州諸軍事、征虜將軍、豫州刺史，餘如故。

translations.literal: Mian was appointed Right Guard General and still made Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Yu and Si provinces' military affairs, General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, and Governor of Yu Province; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was made Right Guard General and also bearer of the staff, commander of Yu and Si, General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, and governor of Yu, with his other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 四年，除侍中，領射聲校尉，又不受。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Palace Attendant and Colonel of the Archers, and again did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was offered palace attendant and colonel of the archers, and again declined.

sentences.zh: 進號右將軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to Right General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right General.

sentences.zh: 其年，虜遣汝陽司馬趙懷仁步騎五百，寇武津縣。

translations.literal: That year the barbarians sent Ruyang Army Major Zhao Huairen with five hundred infantry and cavalry to raid Wujin County.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Wei sent Ruyang army major Zhao Huairen with five hundred horse and foot to raid Wujin County.

sentences.zh: 勔遣龍驤將軍曲元德輕兵進討，虜眾驚散。

translations.literal: Mian sent General of the Dragon Cavalry Qu Yuande with light troops forward in attack, and the barbarian host fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Mian sent General Qu Yuande of the Dragon Cavalry with light troops against them, and the Wei force scattered in alarm.

sentences.zh: 虜子都公閼於拔又率三百人防運車囗囗千兩，於汝陽臺東水上結營。

translations.literal: The barbarian Prince of Zidu Yan Yu again led three hundred men to guard transport wagons [text missing] thousand loads and encamped east of the water at Ruyang Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei prince Yan Yu of Zidu then led three hundred men to guard a train of transport wagons and camped on the east bank below Ruyang Terrace.

sentences.zh: 元德單騎直入，斬拔首，因進攻汝陽臺，即陷外壘，獲車一千三百乘，斬首一百五十級。

translations.literal: Yuande alone on horseback charged straight in, beheaded Ba, then attacked Ruyang Terrace, at once taking the outer rampart, capturing thirteen hundred wagons, and taking one hundred fifty heads.
translations.idiomatic: Yuande charged in alone, cut off Ba's head, then stormed Ruyang Terrace, took the outer works at once, seized thirteen hundred wagons, and took a hundred and fifty heads.

sentences.zh: 勔又使司徒參軍孫曇瓘督弋陽以西，會虜寇義陽，曇瓘大破之。

translations.literal: Mian also had Secretariat Army Staff Officer Sun Tanhuan command west of Yiyang; when the barbarians raided Yiyang, Tanhuan routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Mian also put Secretariat staff officer Sun Tanhuan in command west of Yiyang; when the Wei struck Yiyang, Tanhuan defeated them decisively.

sentences.zh: 虜上其北豫州租，有車二千兩，勔招荒人，邀擊於許昌，虜眾奔散，焚燒米穀。

translations.literal: The barbarians were transporting their Northern Yu Province tax grain with two thousand wagons; Mian recruited frontier people and ambushed them at Xuchang; the barbarian host fled and scattered, burning grain and rice.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei were moving two thousand cartloads of Northern Yu tax grain; Mian rallied frontier men and ambushed them at Xuchang; the Wei force fled and burned its grain.

sentences.zh: 淮西人賈元友上書太宗，勸北攻懸瓠，可收陳郡、南頓、汝南、新蔡四郡之地。

translations.literal: Jia Yuanyou of Huai West memorialized Emperor Ming urging a northern attack on Xuanhu, by which the lands of the four commanderies Chen, Nandun, Runan, and Xincai could be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yuanyou of the Huai West region memorialized the emperor urging a northern strike on Xuanhu to recover Chen, Nandun, Runan, and Xincai.

sentences.zh: 上以所陳示勔，使具條答。

translations.literal: The emperor showed what had been stated to Mian and had him answer item by item.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed Mian the memorial and told him to reply point by point.

sentences.zh: 勔對曰：

translations.literal: Mian replied:
translations.idiomatic: Mian replied:

sentences.zh: 元友稱：「虜主幼弱，姦偽競起，內外規亂，天亡有期。

translations.literal: Yuanyou states: "The barbarian lord is young and weak; treachery and deceit rise in rivalry; within and without they plot disorder; heaven's destruction has its term."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou claims: "The Wei ruler is young and weak, treachery is rampant, the realm is in turmoil within and without, and their fall is only a matter of time."

sentences.zh: 」臣以為獯醜侵縱，乘藉王境，盤據州郡，百姓殘亡。

translations.literal: " Your servant holds that the Xiongnu-like foe invades wantonly, treading the royal domain, entrenched in provinces and commanderies, and the people are ruined and perishing.
translations.idiomatic: " I believe the barbarians are still raiding at will, trampling our territory, holding whole provinces, and the people are being destroyed.

sentences.zh: 去冬眾軍失耕，今春連城圍逼，國家復境之略，實有不遑，滅虜未及。

translations.literal: Last winter the armies lost their planting; this spring linked cities are pressed by siege; the state's plan to recover the borders truly has no leisure; destroying the barbarians is not yet possible.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter our armies missed the planting season; this spring walled towns are under siege; the court can hardly keep up with recovering lost territory, let alone destroying the Wei.

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「有七千餘家，穀米豐積，可供二萬人數年資儲。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also says: "There are more than seven thousand households with grain and rice in rich store, enough to supply twenty thousand men for several years."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also says: "More than seven thousand households have abundant grain, enough to feed twenty thousand men for years."

sentences.zh: 」臣又以為二萬人歲食米四十八萬斛，五年合須米二百四十萬斛，既理不容有，恐事難稱言。

translations.literal: " Your servant further holds that twenty thousand men yearly consume four hundred eighty thousand hu of rice; in five years together two million four hundred thousand hu would be needed; since reason does not allow this to exist, I fear the matter is hard to square with words.
translations.idiomatic: " I further calculate that twenty thousand men would consume four hundred and eighty thousand bushels of rice a year, or two million four hundred thousand over five years; such stores are impossible, and I fear his claims will not bear scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「虜於懸瓠開驛保，虜已先據，若不足恃，此不須囗。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also says: "The barbarians opened relay stations and forts at Xuanhu; the barbarians already hold them first; if they are not reliable to depend on, this need not be [considered]."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also says: "The Wei have opened relay stations at Xuanhu and already hold them; if those cannot be relied on, this point need not be pursued."

sentences.zh: 」俱是攻城，便應先圖懸瓠，何更越先取郾，以受腹背之災。

translations.literal: " Since all are siege warfare, one ought first to plan for Xuanhu; why further leap ahead first to take Yan and suffer disaster from front and rear?
translations.idiomatic: " If we are besieging cities, we should take Xuanhu first; why strike Yan ahead of it and expose ourselves to attack from both sides?

sentences.zh: 且七千餘家豐積，而虜猶當遠運為糧，是威不制民，民非異計。

translations.literal: Moreover, though more than seven thousand households have rich stores, the barbarians still must transport grain from afar for provisions—this shows their authority does not control the people, and the people are not of a different plan.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if seven thousand households truly had such stores, the Wei would not still be hauling grain from far away; their rule does not command the people, and the people are not on their side.

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「虜欲水陸運糧，以救軍命，可襲之機，在於今日。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also says: "The barbarians wish to transport grain by water and land to save the army's life; the chance to strike lies in today."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also says: "The Wei plan to move grain by land and water to save their armies; the moment to strike is now."

sentences.zh: 」臣又以為開立驛道，據守堅城，觀其形候，不似蹙弱。

translations.literal: " Your servant further holds that they have opened relay roads and hold strong cities; observing their form and signs, they do not seem pressed and weak.
translations.idiomatic: " I further note that they have opened relay routes and hold fortified towns; by every sign they do not look desperate or weak.

sentences.zh: 可乘之機，恐為難驗。

translations.literal: The chance to exploit may be hard to verify.
translations.idiomatic: The opening he describes may be impossible to confirm.

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「四郡民人，遭虜二十七年之毒，皆欲雪仇報恥，伏待朝威。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also says: "The people of the four commanderies, having suffered the barbarians' poison for twenty-seven years, all wish to wash away shame and avenge insult, bowing to await the court's majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also says: "The people of the four commanderies have suffered under the Wei for twenty-seven years; they all long to avenge their wrongs and await the court's authority."

sentences.zh: 」臣又以為垣式寶等受國重恩，今猶驅略車營，翻還就賊，蓋是戀本之情深，非報怨之宜，何可輕試。

translations.literal: " Your servant further holds that Yuan Shibao and others received the state's heavy grace, yet still drive off and plunder wagon camps and turn back to join the enemy—likely their attachment to their homeland runs deep, not that they are fit to avenge wrongs; how can one lightly test this?
translations.idiomatic: " I would add that men like Yuan Shibao received great favor from the state, yet still raid supply trains and go back to the enemy; they love their old homes, not our cause. How can we trust such men lightly?

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「請敕荊、雍兩州，遣二千精兵，從義陽依西山北下，直據郾城。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also says: "Please order Jing and Yong provinces to send two thousand elite troops from Yiyang along the western hills northward, directly seizing Yan City."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also asks that Jing and Yong be ordered to send two thousand picked troops from Yiyang down the western hills to seize Yan City at once.

sentences.zh: 」臣又以為郾城是賊驛路要戍，且經蠻接險，數百里中，裹糧潛進，方出平地，攻賊堅城，自古名將，未有能以此濟者。

translations.literal: " Your servant further holds that Yan City is a key garrison on the enemy relay route, and the route passes through barbarian lands and perilous terrain; for several hundred li, carrying grain in secret advance, only then reaching open ground to attack the enemy's strong city—from antiquity's famous generals, none has succeeded by this means.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan is a vital post on the enemy relay line, and the route runs through barbarian country and rough terrain. To march several hundred li on secret rations, then emerge onto open ground and storm a walled town—no famous general in history has ever made such a plan work.

sentences.zh: 假其克捷，不知足南抗懸瓠，北捍長社與不？

translations.literal: Even if they achieved victory, one does not know whether it would suffice to resist Xuanhu in the south and hold Changshe in the north or not.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they won, could they hold off Xuanhu to the south and Changshe to the north?

sentences.zh: 且賊擁據數城，水陸通便，而今使官以二千斷其資運，於事為難。

translations.literal: Moreover, the enemy holds several cities with convenient water and land routes; now to have officials with two thousand cut off their supplies and transport is difficult in practice.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy hold several cities with easy communications by land and water; to cut their supplies with only two thousand men is hardly feasible.

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「虜圍逼汝陰，遊魂二歲，為張景遠所挫，不敢渡淮。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also says: "The barbarians besieged Yuyin for two years as wandering souls, were checked by Zhang Jingyuan, and dared not cross the Huai."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also says: "The Wei besieged Yuyin for two years, were beaten back by Zhang Jingyuan, and dare not cross the Huai."

sentences.zh: 」臣又以為景遠兵力寡弱，不能自固，遠遣救援，方得少克。

translations.literal: " Your servant further holds that Jingyuan's force was few and weak and could not secure himself; only by sending relief from afar did he achieve a small victory.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingyuan's force was small and weak; he could not hold on alone and only won a minor success when relief reached him from far away.

sentences.zh: 今定是為賊所畏不？

translations.literal: Is he now certainly feared by the enemy or not?
translations.idiomatic: Are the enemy truly afraid of him now?

sentences.zh: 景遠前所摧傷，裁至數百，虜步騎四萬，猶不敢前，而今必勸國家以輕兵遠討，指掌可克，言理相背，莫復過此。

translations.literal: The damage Jingyuan inflicted before amounted to only several hundred; the barbarians had forty thousand foot and horse yet still dared not advance—yet now he must urge the state to campaign far with light troops, conquerable at a gesture; words and reason oppose each other—nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan's earlier blows killed only a few hundred; forty thousand Wei horse and foot still would not advance—yet now we are told a light force can march far and win at a snap. Nothing could be more contrary to reason.

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「龍山雉水，魯奴、王景直等並受朝爵，馬步萬餘。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also says: "At Longshan and Zhi River, Lu Nu, Wang Jingzhi, and others all received court ranks, with more than ten thousand horse and foot."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also says: "At Longshan and Zhi River, Lu Nu, Wang Jingzhi, and others all hold court titles and command more than ten thousand horse and foot."

sentences.zh: 進討之宜，唯須敕命。

translations.literal: The fitness for advancing in attack requires only an imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: They are ready to advance; all that is needed is an imperial command.

sentences.zh: 」臣以為魯奴與虜交關，彌歷年世，去歲送誠朝廷，誓欲立功。

translations.literal: " Your servant holds that Lu Nu has had dealings with the barbarians spanning many years; last year he sent sincerity to the court, vowing to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Nu has dealt with the Wei for years; only last year he professed loyalty to the court and vowed to serve.

sentences.zh: 自蒙榮爵，便即逃遁，殊類姦猾，豈易闇期。

translations.literal: Once he received honored rank, he at once fled; such a type is treacherous and cunning—how can one easily count on him in secret?
translations.idiomatic: Once he received his titles he fled at once. Men so treacherous cannot be trusted in advance.

sentences.zh: 兼王景直是一亡命，部曲不過數十人，既不可言，又未足恃。

translations.literal: Moreover, Wang Jingzhi is a mere fugitive; his followers number no more than several tens—he can neither be spoken of nor relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: As for Wang Jingzhi, he is only a fugitive with a few dozen men—not worth mentioning and not to be relied on.

sentences.zh: 萬餘之言，似不近實。

translations.literal: The talk of more than ten thousand seems not close to fact.
translations.idiomatic: The claim of ten thousand men hardly seems real.

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「四郡恨忿此非類，車營連結，廢田二載，生業已盡，賊無所資，糧儲已罄。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also says: "The four commanderies hate and resent these alien kinds; wagon camps link in chains; fields lie waste for two years; livelihoods are exhausted; the rebels have nothing to draw on; grain stores are empty."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also says: "The four commanderies hate the barbarians; their supply trains are strung together; fields have lain fallow for two years; livelihoods are gone; the enemy have no resources left and their granaries are empty."

sentences.zh: 斷其運道，最是要略。

translations.literal: Cutting their transport routes is the most essential strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting their supply lines is the key move.

sentences.zh: 」臣又以斷運須兵，兵應資食，而當此過懸瓠二百里中，使兵食兼足，何處求辦？

translations.literal: " Your servant further holds that cutting transport requires troops, and troops need provisions—yet in this stretch of two hundred li past Xuanhu, to make both troops and food sufficient, where is one to obtain them?
translations.idiomatic: " Cutting supplies takes troops, and troops need food. In two hundred li beyond Xuanhu, where are we to find enough of both?

sentences.zh: 臣竊尋元嘉以來，傖荒遠人，多干國議，負儋歸闕，皆勸討虜。

translations.literal: Your servant privately reviews that since Yuanjia, northern frontier people from distant lands have often interfered in state counsel, bearing loads to return to court, all urging campaigns against the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuanjia, frontier people from the far north have often pressed themselves on court policy, coming to the capital laden with gifts, all urging campaigns against the Wei.

sentences.zh: 魯爽誕說，實挫國威，徒失兵力，虛費金寶。

translations.literal: The schemes of Lu Shuang and Dan truly damaged national prestige, vainly losing military strength and wasting gold and treasure.
translations.idiomatic: The plans urged by men like Lu Shuang and Prince Dan truly damaged our prestige, cost us troops for nothing, and wasted treasure.

sentences.zh: 凡此之徒，每規近說，從來信納，皆詒後悔。

translations.literal: All such types each plot near-term proposals; whenever the court has believed and adopted them, it has afterward regretted.
translations.idiomatic: Such men always offer short-term schemes; whenever the court has listened, it has later regretted doing so.

sentences.zh: 界上之人，唯視強弱，王師至境，必壺漿候塗，裁見退軍，便抄截蜂起。

translations.literal: People on the borders look only to strength and weakness; when royal troops reach the frontier they surely bring jars of drink to await on the road—but at the mere sight of withdrawing armies, raiding and ambush rise like bees.
translations.idiomatic: Border folk watch only who is strong; when imperial troops arrive they greet them with wine on the road, but the moment an army retreats they swarm out to plunder.

sentences.zh: 首領回師，何嘗不為河畔所弊。

translations.literal: When commanders lead the army back, when have they not been harmed along the riverbanks?
translations.idiomatic: How often have returning commanders not been harried along the rivers?

sentences.zh: 太宗納之，元友議遂寢。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming accepted this; Yuanyou's proposal then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Mian's view, and Yuanyou's plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 勔與常珍奇書，勸令反虜，珍奇乃與子超越、羽林監式寶，於譙殺虜子都公費拔等凡三千餘人。

translations.literal: Mian wrote to Chang Zhenqi urging him to turn against the barbarians; Zhenqi then with his son Chaoyue and Forest of Feathers Guard Shibao at Qiao killed the barbarian Prince of Zidu Fei Ba and others, altogether more than three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Mian wrote to Chang Zhenqi urging him to turn on the Wei; Zhenqi, his son Chaoyue, and guard officer Shibao then killed the Wei prince Fei Ba and more than three thousand men at Qiao.

sentences.zh: 勔馳驛以聞，太宗大喜，以珍奇為使持節、都督司、北豫二州諸軍事、平北將軍、司州刺史，汝南、新蔡縣侯，食邑千戶；

translations.literal: Mian sent word by post relay; Emperor Ming was greatly pleased and made Zhenqi Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Si and Northern Yu provinces' military affairs, General Who Pacifies the North, Governor of Si Province, Marquis of Runan and Xincai counties with a fief of one thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Mian reported by express courier; the emperor was delighted and made Zhenqi bearer of the staff, commander of Si and Northern Yu, General Who Pacifies the North, governor of Si, and marquis of Runan and Xincai with a fief of one thousand households;

sentences.zh: 超越輔國將軍、北豫州刺史，潁川、汝陽、囗囗三郡太守，安陽縣男；

translations.literal: Chaoyue was made General Who Assists the State and Governor of Northern Yu Province, Governor of the three commanderies Yingchuan, Ruyang, and [text missing], and Baron of Anyang County;
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyue was made General Who Assists the State and governor of Northern Yu, governor of Yingchuan, Ruyang, and a third commandery, and baron of Anyang;

sentences.zh: 式寶輔國將軍、陳、南頓二郡太守，真陽縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Shibao was made General Who Assists the State and Governor of the two commanderies Chen and Nandun, Baron of Zhenyang County with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Shibao was made General Who Assists the State, governor of Chen and Nandun, and baron of Zhenyang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 珍奇為虜所攻，引軍南出，虜追擊破之，珍奇走依山，得至壽陽，超越、式寶為人所殺。

translations.literal: Zhenqi was attacked by the barbarians, led his army southward, the barbarians pursued and defeated him; Zhenqi fled into the hills and reached Shouyang; Chaoyue and Shibao were killed by others.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei attacked Zhenqi; he marched south, was pursued and beaten, fled into the hills, and reached Shouyang; Chaoyue and Shibao were killed.

sentences.zh: 五年，汝陰太守楊文萇又頻破虜於荊亭及戍西。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Yuyin Governor Yang Wenchang again repeatedly defeated the barbarians at Jingting and West Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Yang Wenchang of Yuyin again defeated the Wei repeatedly at Jingting and the western garrison.

sentences.zh: 詔進勔號平西將軍、豫州刺史，餘如故，不拜。

translations.literal: An edict advanced Mian's title to General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yu Province, the rest unchanged; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to General Who Pacifies the West and governor of Yu, with his other posts unchanged; he declined.

sentences.zh: 其年，徵拜散騎常侍、中領軍。

translations.literal: That year he was summoned and appointed Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was recalled as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and central army commander.

sentences.zh: 勔以世路糾紛，有懷止足，求東陽郡。

translations.literal: Mian, seeing the world's paths tangled, cherished the wish to know when to stop and requested Dongyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: With the times in turmoil, Mian wished to know when enough was enough and asked to be sent to Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 上以勔啟遍示朝臣，自尚書僕射袁粲以下，莫不稱讚，咸謂宜許。

translations.literal: The emperor showed Mian's memorial throughout to the court ministers; from Secretariat Vice Director Yuan Can downward, none failed to praise it, all saying it should be granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor circulated Mian's request to the whole court; from Vice Director Yuan Can down, everyone praised it and said it should be granted.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「巴陵、建平二王，並有獨往之志。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The two princes of Baling and Jianping both have the will to go their own way.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The princes of Baling and Jianping both have minds of their own.

sentences.zh: 若世道寧晏，皆當申其所請。

translations.literal: If the age's way becomes peaceful and tranquil, all should have their requests granted."
translations.idiomatic: When the realm is at peace, each of them shall have what he asks."

sentences.zh: 」勔經始鍾嶺之南，以為棲息，聚石蓄水，仿佛丘中，朝士愛素者，多往遊之。

translations.literal: " Mian began construction south of Zhong Ridge as his dwelling, gathering stones and storing water, resembling a hill retreat; court gentlemen who loved simplicity often went to visit.
translations.idiomatic: " Mian built an estate south of Zhong Ridge, piling stones and storing water in the manner of a mountain retreat; many officials who loved a simple life visited him there.

sentences.zh: 六年，改常侍為侍中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year his Regular Attendant post was changed to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year his title of regular attendant was changed to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 其年，南兗州刺史齊王出鎮淮陰，以勔為使持節、都督南徐、兗、青、冀、囗五州諸軍事、平北將軍，侍中、中領軍如故，出鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: That year, when Southern Yanzhou Governor the Prince of Qi went out to garrison Huaiyin, Mian was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Southern Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and [missing] five provinces' military affairs, General Who Pacifies the North, Palace Attendant and Central Army Commander as before, and went out to garrison Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when the Prince of Qi left to hold Huaiyin as governor of Southern Yan, Mian was made bearer of the staff, commander of five provinces including Southern Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji, General Who Pacifies the North, and kept his posts as palace attendant and central army commander while going out to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 固辭侍中、軍號，許之，以為假平北將軍。

translations.literal: He firmly declined Palace Attendant and the army title; this was granted, and he was made acting General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the posts of palace attendant and full general; the court agreed and made him acting General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 七年，解都督、假號、并節。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was relieved of command, acting title, and the staff together.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was relieved of his command, acting rank, and staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 太宗臨崩，顧命以為守尚書右僕射，中領軍如故，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: As Emperor Ming lay dying, he entrusted him as Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, Central Army Commander unchanged, and granted one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Emperor Ming named him acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, kept him as central army commander, and granted him a full guard of honor musicians.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，加兵五百人。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, five hundred troops were added to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, his guard was increased by five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，月犯右執法，太白犯上將，或勸勔解職。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanhui, the moon trespassed on the Right Enforcer and Venus trespassed on the Great General; some urged Mian to resign his office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhui, when omens appeared in the sky, some urged Mian to resign.

sentences.zh: 勔曰：「吾執心行己，無愧幽明。

translations.literal: Mian said: "In holding my heart and conducting myself, I have no shame before the hidden and the manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Mian said: "In heart and conduct I have nothing to fear before heaven or earth.

sentences.zh: 若才輕任重，災眚必及，天道密微，避豈得免。

translations.literal: If talent is light and burden heavy, calamity must reach one; heaven's way is subtle and hidden—by avoiding can one escape?"
translations.idiomatic: If my talent is slight for my burden, disaster will find me; heaven's ways are secret—what escape is there?"

sentences.zh: 」桂陽王休範為亂，奄至京邑，加勔使持節、領軍，置佐史，鎮扞石頭。

translations.literal: " When Prince of Guiyang Xiufan rebelled and suddenly reached the capital district, Mian was additionally made Bearer of the Staff and Army Commander, staff officers appointed, garrisoning and defending Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: " When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled and swept on the capital, Mian was given the staff, made army commander with a full staff, and posted to defend Stone City.

sentences.zh: 既而賊眾屯朱雀航南，右軍王道隆率宿衛向朱雀，聞賊已至，急信召勔。

translations.literal: Soon after, the rebel host camped south of the Vermilion Bird Ford; Right Army Wang Daolong led the palace guard toward the Vermilion Bird; hearing the rebels had arrived, he urgently summoned Mian by message.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then camped south of Vermilion Bird Ford; Wang Daolong of the Right Army led the palace guard toward the ford and, hearing the enemy had arrived, urgently summoned Mian.

sentences.zh: 勔至，命閉航，道隆不聽，催勔渡航進戰。

translations.literal: When Mian arrived he ordered the ford closed; Daolong would not listen and urged Mian to cross the ford and advance to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Mian arrived and ordered the ford closed; Daolong refused and pressed him to cross and fight.

sentences.zh: 率所領於航南戰敗，臨陳死之，時年五十七。

translations.literal: Leading those under his command he was defeated south of the ford and died in the battle line, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men to battle south of the ford, was defeated, and died in the front line at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 事平，詔曰：「夫義實天經，忠惟人則，篆素流采，金石宣輝，自非識洞情靈，理感生極，豈有捐軀衛主，捨命匡朝者哉！

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, an edict said: "Righteousness is truly heaven's constant; loyalty is man's rule; seal-script and silk stream with color, metal and stone proclaim splendor—from antiquity unless one penetrates feeling and spirit and reason touches life's utmost, how could there be those who cast off the body to guard the lord and abandon life to steady the court!"
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored, an edict said: "Righteousness is heaven's law and loyalty mankind's standard; only one who truly knows the heart and feels life's deepest truth will give his body to guard his sovereign and his life to save the dynasty!"

sentences.zh: 故持節、鎮軍將軍、守尚書右僕射、中領軍鄱陽縣開國侯勔，思懷亮粹，體業淹明，弘勳樹績，譽洽華野。

translations.literal: The late Bearer of the Staff, General Who Garrisons the Army, Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, Central Army Commander, and Enfeoffed Marquis of Poyang County Mian—his thought and bosom were bright and pure, his substance and achievement broad and clear; he spread great merit and raised achievement, his fame filling court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: The late Bearer of the Staff, General Who Garrisons the Army, Acting Right Vice Director, Central Army Commander, and Enfeoffed Marquis of Poyang, Liu Mian, was pure in mind and brilliant in bearing; his deeds were great and his fame filled the land.

sentences.zh: 綢繆顧託，契闊屯夷，方倚謀猷，翌康帝道。

translations.literal: Bound close in entrusted care, sharing hardship in perilous times, we were just relying on his counsel to assist and bring peace to the imperial way.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with the realm in hard times, we had leaned on his counsel to steady the throne.

sentences.zh: 逆蕃扇禍，逼擾京甸，援桴誓旅，奉律行師。

translations.literal: The rebellious barbarian fanned calamity, pressing and disturbing the capital region; he took up the drumstick and pledged the host, upholding law in leading the army.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion threatened the capital, he took up arms and led his troops forth under the law of war.

sentences.zh: 身與事滅，名隨操遠。

translations.literal: His person perished with the affair; his name follows his conduct into the distance.
translations.idiomatic: His body fell with the cause, but his name endures with his conduct.

sentences.zh: 朕用傷悼，震慟於厥心。

translations.literal: We therefore grieve and mourn, shaken in Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: We are stricken with grief and shaken to the heart.

sentences.zh: 昔王允秉誠，卞壼峻節，均風往德，歸茂先軌。

translations.literal: Formerly Wang Yun held sincerity and Bian Hu had stern integrity; equal in wind with past virtue, returning to adorn the former track.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun of old was steadfast and Bian Hu was stern in integrity; Mian stands with them among the great exemplars of the past.

sentences.zh: 泉途就永，冤逝無追，思崇徽策，式光惇史。

translations.literal: The spring road reaches eternity; wronged departure has no recall; We think to exalt his fine policy and thereby glorify the sincere histories.
translations.idiomatic: He has gone to the eternal road beyond recall; We would honor him with noble titles and set his glory in the histories.

sentences.zh: 可贈散騎常侍、司空，本官、侯如故，諡曰忠昭公。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously given Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and Minister of Works, his original offices and marquisate unchanged; his posthumous title shall be Duke Zhongzhao."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and Minister of Works, with his offices and marquisate unchanged, and let his posthumous title be Loyal and Illustrious Duke."

sentences.zh: 子悛嗣，順帝升明末，為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Juan succeeded; at the end of the Shengming era under Emperor Shun he was Governor of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Juan succeeded to the title; late in the Shengming era under Emperor Shun he became governor of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi dynasty took the throne, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 勔弟斅，泰始中，為寧朔將軍、交州刺史，於道遇病卒。

translations.literal: Mian's younger brother Jiao, in the Taishi era, was General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Jiao Province; on the road he met illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: Mian's younger brother Jiao served in Taishi as General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Jiao, but died of illness on the way to his post.

sentences.zh: 先有都鄉侯爵，諡曰質侯。

translations.literal: He earlier had the rank of Marquis of Duxiang; his posthumous title was Marquis Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier held the rank of marquis of Duxiang; his posthumous title was Marquis Zhi.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：吳漢平蜀，城內流血沾踝，而其後無聞於漢；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When Wu Han pacified Shu, blood in the city reached the ankles, yet afterward he was unheard of in Han;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When Wu Han conquered Shu, blood in the city reached men's ankles, yet afterward he vanished from Han history;

sentences.zh: 陸抗定西陵，步氏禍及嬰孩，而機、雲為戮上國。

translations.literal: when Lu Kang secured Xiling, the Bu clan's calamity reached infants in arms, yet Ji and Yun were executed in the upper state.
translations.idiomatic: when Lu Kang took Xiling, the Bu clan's punishment reached infants in arms, yet Lu Ji and Lu Yun were put to death by the Jin;

sentences.zh: 劉勔克壽春，士民無遺芻委粒之歎；

translations.literal: when Liu Mian took Shouchun, gentlemen and commoners had no lament of scattered fodder and grain;
translations.idiomatic: when Liu Mian took Shouchun, the people did not mourn lost grain and fodder;

sentences.zh: 莫不扶老攜幼，歌唱而出重圍，美矣！

translations.literal: none failed to support the old and lead the young, singing as they came out of the heavy encirclement—beautiful indeed!
translations.idiomatic: everyone came out of the siege supporting the old and leading the young, singing as they went—a thing of beauty indeed!
